newsitem.title: UK: Labour plans to surrender to EU - Britain's Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: Labour plans to surrender to EU - Britain's Rifkind.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, reacting to Labour pledges to build closer links with the European Union, on Friday accused the opposition party of planning "six surrenders in six weeks" if it came to power.

He was commenting on a visit to Brussels on Thursday by Labour's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook during which he said Labour should be able to agree a new EU Treaty at a summit meeting soon after an imminent British election.
"Labour are more concerned with courting popularity in Brussels than standing up for Britain in Europe," he said.
The June 16-17 summit, in Amsterdam, is due to conclude the Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) which has been set up to agree changes in the operation of the bloc.

No date has been formally fixed for the election in Britain, but Prime Minister John Major has dropped broad hints that it will be on May 1. Opinion polls show Labour more than 20 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives.

Cook said on Thursday, after meeting EU Commission President Jacques Santer, that Labour would end Britain's opt-out from the Social Chapter, which deals with employment rights, and drop the Conservatives' threat to block the whole IGC treaty unless Britain were exempted from EU rules on the maximum working week.

He also said Labour would consider, on a case-by-case basis, proposals to end member states' vetoes in key areas of decision taking, allowing new regulations to be adopted on the basis of a qualified majority voting system.
Rifkind said Labour would give up the veto in four areas -- regional, social, industrial and environment policy -- adding to its concessions on employment rights and the working week.

"Their six surrenders in six weeks policy would massively undermine Britain's national interest," he said in a statement. "Robin Cook yesterday confirmed the worst fears of the damage a Labour government would inflict on Britain at the IGC in Amsterdam if they were to represent the United Kingdom there."
